sections.text: When to Visit Kenya Kenya is a year-round destination, with each season offering something uniquely captivating. From July to October, the Great Migration transforms the Maasai Mara into a living epic, while the dry months (January to March) deliver crisp air and crystal-clear game viewing. The green seasons bring life to the land, fewer crowds, and dramatic photographic opportunities. Learn more about seasons here.

Choose from private conservancy stays, family-friendly adventures, or romantic fly-in safaris that combine wilderness and coast. Each journey is crafted to immerse you in Africa's most iconic safari experiences. Learn more about tours here.

Temperature and rainfall do vary depending on the altitude and terrain. There are 2 rainy seasons. A short one from late October through the end of November, and a long one from March to early June. cards.text: Do I need a visa to travel to Kenya? People coming for Kenya safari holidays, or Kenya safari tours will need a Visitor Visa which they can apply for here . Until recently visitors from many countries were able to obtain a visa on arrival. However, as of January 1, 2021, that is no longer the case and everyone must apply via the online application form before arriving in the country. Check the application form page for a full list of required documents for your safari trip.

cards.cls: group/accordion-item
cards.text: What languages are spoken in Kenya? The official languages are Swahili and English. For business, government, and tourism, English is in common use. At lodges, resorts, and in major cities, English is widespread. Swahili is the predominant indigenous language. Learning a few key phrases, such as Jambo (Hello), Kwaheri (Good bye), Hakuna Matata (No worries)… will enhance your travel experience, connecting you with the local people.

cards.cls: group/accordion-item
cards.text: What currency is used in Kenya? The Kenyan Shilling (KES) is the official currency of Kenya. In tourist areas, US dollars are routinely accepted, so too when making larger purchases. Carry some local currency, to be used for smaller purchases and gratuities. ATMs are common in major town centers. Credit cards are accepted in large retail stores, restaurants, and all hotels/resorts while on your Kenya Safari.

cards.text: When is the best time to go on a Tanzania Safari? The most popular time to visit is from June to October during the dry season. Clear skies and minimal rain make it ideal for both safari and beach vacations. The wet season (November to May) sees fewer tourists, lush scenery, and better birdwatching. While better when dry, wildlife sightings are good throughout the year.

cards.cls: group/accordion-item
cards.text: Do I need a visa to travel to Tanzania? Most tourists need an Ordinary Visa. First determine whether you need to obtain this prior to arrival via Tanzania diplomatic missions, or an online eVisa. For some nationalities, visas are issued at the point of entry (international airport or border post). Visitors from the USA, and those who will visit other neighboring countries before departing Tanzania, must obtain a Multiple-Entry Visa. Always check the latest visa requirements before traveling.
